title: Metamaterials concept-learning research dataset
scope: Nine families spanning mechanical, acoustic and optical metamaterials; variants are named, mechanisms are concise, and biological inspiration is not inferred from visual resemblance.

evidence_status_legend.experimentally_demonstrated: Primary source reports a fabricated or physical experimental realization.
evidence_status_legend.analytical_and_numerical: Primary source develops theory and/or simulation without the same claim being physically demonstrated there.
evidence_status_legend.conceptual_foundation: Seminal theoretical proposal or foundational classification.

families.name: Auxetic lattices
families.core_idea: A geometry-dominated solid with effective Poisson ratio nu_eff < 0: it widens under axial tension.

variants.name: Re-entrant foam / re-entrant honeycomb

inspiration.basis: Inward-pointing cell ribs rotate and bend; the cited foam was transformed from conventional open-cell foam.

variants.mechanism: Opening of re-entrant cell angles couples axial extension to transverse expansion.
limitations: response depends on strain range and buckling

variants.name: Rotating squares

inspiration.basis: Rigid squares joined at vertices form a rotating-unit mechanism.

variants.mechanism: Counter-rotation of nearly rigid squares opens gaps in both axes; the ideal mechanism approaches nu = -1.
limitations: ideal hinges are difficult to realize

families.name: Origami and kirigami metamaterials
families.core_idea: Creases or cuts prescribe low-energy deformation paths, enabling large shape change from thin sheets.
families.key_relation: Rigid-origami compatibility constrains fold angles; mobility follows the crease-pattern constraint rank.

variants.name: Miura-ori

inspiration.basis: Periodic parallelogram crease pattern developed by Koryo Miura.

variants.mechanism: One-degree-of-freedom rigid folding couples in-plane dimensions and produces tunable anisotropy and negative Poisson response.

variants.name: X-shaped tristable kirigami

inspiration.basis: Engineered X-shaped cuts create coupled snap-through units.

variants.mechanism: Cut ligaments buckle and snap between three stable configurations; hierarchy propagates programmed shape changes.

families.name: Extreme-stiffness elastic lattices
families.core_idea: Architecture steers which elastic moduli remain large or small, producing unusual effective elasticity.
families.key_relation: Pentamode target: bulk modulus B much greater than shear modulus G; figure of merit B/G.

variants.name: Double-cone pentamode lattice

inspiration.basis: Pentamode theory leaves one nonzero eigenvalue in the 6x6 elasticity tensor.

variants.mechanism: Point-like connections between double cones resist compression far more than shear, approximating a solid that flows acoustically like a fluid.
limitations: finite junctions give nonzero shear modulus

variants.name: Isotropic plate-nanolattice

inspiration.basis: Plate-based unit cells were designed to approach Hashin-Shtrikman isotropic stiffness bounds.

variants.mechanism: Material placed in intersecting plates carries load primarily by stretching rather than beam bending.

families.name: Locally resonant acoustic metamaterials
families.core_idea: Subwavelength resonators exchange momentum or compressibility with the host and can create stop bands below the Bragg scale.
families.key_relation: Near resonance, effective density or bulk modulus can become dispersive and negative; a mass-spring resonance obeys omega_0 = sqrt(k/m).

variants.name: Coated-sphere sonic crystal

inspiration.basis: Dense cores and compliant coatings act as local mass-spring resonators.

variants.mechanism: Core motion out of phase with the matrix yields negative effective dynamic mass near resonance and a low-frequency band gap.

variants.name: Membrane-plus-Helmholtz double-negative cell

inspiration.basis: Membrane resonance controls dynamic density; cavity-neck resonance controls compressibility.

variants.mechanism: Overlapping membrane and Helmholtz resonances produce frequency ranges with simultaneously negative effective density and bulk modulus.

families.name: Phononic crystals and elastic band-gap lattices
families.core_idea: Periodic contrast and interference shape dispersion omega(k), forbidding propagation in selected frequency intervals.
families.key_relation: Bragg gaps occur when wavelength is comparable to lattice spacing; Bloch condition u(r+R)=u(r)exp(i k·R).

variants.name: Bragg-scattering phononic crystal

inspiration.basis: Elastic analogue of electronic and photonic Bloch bands in periodic crystals.

variants.mechanism: Multiple scattering from a periodic array destructively interferes, opening complete or directional band gaps.

variants.name: Inertially amplified lattice

inspiration.basis: Linkages amplify resonator acceleration without simply increasing attached mass.

variants.mechanism: Geometric amplification increases effective inertia and can open deep-subwavelength elastic band gaps.
limitations: hinge compliance and damping shift the gap

families.name: Topological mechanical metamaterials
families.core_idea: A bulk band invariant predicts boundary or interface modes that persist under disorder that does not close the relevant band gap or break required symmetry.
families.key_relation: Bulk-boundary correspondence links a winding/Chern/polarization invariant to edge-mode count.

variants.name: Topological Maxwell lattice

inspiration.basis: Maxwell isostatic frames combined with a topological polarization of the compatibility matrix.

variants.mechanism: Changing unit-cell geometry shifts floppy modes to one boundary and states of self-stress to the opposite boundary.
limitations: protection is conditional on gap and symmetry

variants.name: Gyroscopic Chern lattice

inspiration.basis: Spinning gyroscopes break time-reversal symmetry and realize a mechanical analogue of Chern bands.

variants.mechanism: Gyroscopic precession produces nonreciprocal coupling and one-way edge waves around defects.

families.name: Photonic crystals
families.core_idea: Periodic dielectric structure creates optical Bloch bands and photonic band gaps by interference.
families.key_relation: Frequency-domain Maxwell eigenproblem: curl[(1/epsilon(r))curl H] = (omega/c)^2 H.

variants.name: Three-dimensional dielectric photonic crystal

inspiration.basis: Yablonovitch proposed inhibiting spontaneous emission using a periodic dielectric analogue of an electronic band gap.

variants.mechanism: A complete photonic band gap removes propagating optical states over a frequency interval.
limitations: complete 3D gaps need high index contrast

variants.name: Photonic-crystal slab cavity

inspiration.basis: A deliberate defect localizes a mode inside an in-plane photonic band gap.

variants.mechanism: In-plane Bragg confinement plus vertical total internal reflection yields small mode volume and high quality factor.

families.name: Negative-index and hyperbolic metamaterials
families.core_idea: Structured conductors and dielectrics create effective tensor components unavailable together in ordinary transparent media.
families.key_relation: Isotropic negative index requires Re(epsilon)<0 and Re(mu)<0; a uniaxial hyperbolic medium has epsilon_parallel·epsilon_perpendicular<0.

variants.name: Split-ring-and-wire negative-index medium

inspiration.basis: Split rings provide magnetic resonance while wires provide plasma-like electric response.

variants.mechanism: Overlapping negative epsilon and negative mu bands yield backward phase propagation and negative refraction.

variants.name: Metal-dielectric multilayer hyperbolic medium

inspiration.basis: Layer filling fraction tunes opposite signs of principal permittivity components.

variants.mechanism: Indefinite permittivity gives an open hyperbolic isofrequency surface supporting very large in-plane wavevectors.
limitations: nonlocality and finite period cap high-k states

families.name: Optical metasurfaces
families.core_idea: A subwavelength-thin array of scatterers imposes spatially varying phase, amplitude, polarization, or dispersion on a wavefront.
families.key_relation: Generalized refraction adds a phase gradient: n_t sin(theta_t)-n_i sin(theta_i) = (lambda/2pi)dPhi/dx.

variants.name: V-antenna phase-gradient metasurface

inspiration.basis: An engineered array samples a prescribed abrupt phase profile at an interface.

variants.mechanism: Anisotropic plasmonic antennas provide position-dependent cross-polarized phase shifts, steering reflected or transmitted beams.

variants.name: Geometric-phase dielectric metalens

inspiration.basis: Rotating anisotropic nanoelements imparts geometric phase 2theta to converted circular polarization.

variants.mechanism: High-index nanopillars rotate polarization and encode a lens phase profile in a single patterned layer.

variants.name: Huygens dielectric metasurface

inspiration.basis: Balanced electric and magnetic dipole responses act as co-located Huygens sources.

variants.mechanism: Spectrally overlapping electric and magnetic Mie resonances suppress reflection while spanning nearly 2pi transmission phase.
limitations: high-index materials may absorb at some wavelengths

editorial_notes: Metamaterial labels overlap: photonic crystals rely mainly on periodic interference, whereas effective-medium metamaterials rely on subwavelength homogenization; the app should teach this distinction rather than present a rigid taxonomy.
Negative effective parameters are frequency-dependent retrievals, not statements that constituent mass, density, permittivity or permeability is intrinsically negative.
Topological robustness is conditional: disorder can destroy a mode if it closes the gap or breaks the symmetry that protects it.

Natural_derivation is null throughout because these named variants are established through engineering geometry, mathematical physics, or analogy. Do not add biological origin claims based only on visual similarity.
